public_rationale: OpenAI’s April 25, 2023 disclosure confirms that ChatGPT stores conversations and other user data [e1]. On May 6, 2026, Canadian privacy authorities found that OpenAI collects significant amounts of personal information to train its models [e2]. Neither source quantifies ChatGPT’s cumulative personal-data collection through August 7, 2024 or provides comparable totals for earlier collectors, so the claim that the amount was unprecedented remains unresolved [e1, e2].
limitations: Neither source provides historical totals using a consistent definition and unit for personal data [e1, e2].
The May 2026 finding does not establish ChatGPT’s cumulative collection by August 7, 2024 [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: ChatGPT has collected an unprecedented amount of personal data.

statement.excerpt: ChatGPT has gathered unprecedented amounts of personal data
statement.document_title: OpenAI: On a Path to Becoming The World’s Most Frightening Surveillance Company?

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is a historical record in the amount of personal data collected, compared with earlier products or companies.
The claim concerns cumulative collection through publication, rather than collection during a particular quarter.
The latest relevant position is therefore the cumulative amount publicly reportable by August 7, 2024.
Data sensitivity, collection categories, user counts, and total training tokens cannot independently establish the amount of personal data.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable measurements establish that ChatGPT had collected more personal data by the post date than any earlier comparable collection.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable measurements establish that an earlier product or company collected at least as much personal data.
